claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start the assessment, I need to understand your situation with your child/children.

**How old is the child (or oldest child if you have more than one) that you're claiming for?**

Please let me know:
- The age(s) of your child/children
- Their name(s) if you'd like to include them in the assessment

This will help determine which pathway to follow through the eligibility rules. The age is important because it affects whether they can qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my daughter Alex - she's 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have a daughter named **Alex who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, she falls into an automatic qualification category. Let me move forward with the next check in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is she not in paid work at all?**

(This is a standard check for all children - typically for children as young as 8, they wouldn't be working, so I'd expect a "yes" answer, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't work at all - she's only 8! She's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's what I'd expect for an 8-year-old. So Alex is not in paid work, which means she passes this check.

Let me continue with the next step in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now, another standard check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in her own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(Again, for an 8-year-old in primary school, this would typically be "yes" - she wouldn't be receiving these benefits - but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, she doesn't receive any benefits in her own name. She's just a regular 8-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now another check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?**

(For an 8-year-old in primary school, this should be straightforward - she wouldn't be in an apprenticeship - but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's definitely not in an apprenticeship - she's only 8 and still in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! Alex is clearly not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we're at an important stage - checking your residency situation, as this affects Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about your residency status in the UK?**

There are several possible paths here:

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most straightforward path)

2. Or do you have a specific immigration status such as:
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme? (with details about work, studying, jobseeking, etc.)
   - Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since you're living abroad, let me ask a few more questions to understand your specific situation:

**Can you tell me:**

1. **Are you a Crown servant** (e.g., working for the UK government, diplomatic service, armed forces, etc.) living abroad, or are you living abroad for another reason?

2. **If you're not a Crown servant, do you have any immigration status such as settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

3. **What is your connection to the UK?** (For example, are you planning to return, do you have UK citizenship, etc.)

This information will help me determine if you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit, as there are specific circumstances that can qualify someone living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not a Crown servant - I'm just living abroad for personal reasons. I don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme. I'm a UK citizen, but I'm currently based outside the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I understand your situation now - you're a UK citizen living abroad for personal reasons, without any of the special immigration statuses that might allow an exception.

Unfortunately, based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, **normally living in the UK is a requirement for claiming Child Benefit**. Since you're currently living abroad and don't meet any of the special circumstances (Crown servant, EU Settlement Scheme status, etc.), this means you would not meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me navigate to confirm this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the final outcome based on the eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Final Outcome: NOT ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

### Summary:

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at the moment because **you do not meet the UK residency requirement**.

### Why:

While Alex meets all the qualifying criteria for Child Benefit:
- ✅ She is 8 years old (under 16)
- ✅ She is not working
- ✅ She is not receiving benefits in her own right
- ✅ She is not in an apprenticeship

**The key issue is that you, as the claimant, must normally live in the UK to claim Child Benefit.** You are currently living abroad for personal reasons and don't have any special circumstances that would allow an exception (such as being a Crown servant or having settled/pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme with qualifying criteria).

### What You Can Do:

1. **If you return to the UK:** Once you re-establish normal residence in the UK, you would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

2. **For more information:** You can contact HMRC's Child Benefit team or visit [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility) for further guidance.

3. **Other support abroad:** You may want to check what child support is available in the country where you're currently living.

Is there anything else I can help you with, or any other questions about this outcome?

Therefore, Alex is ineligible for Child Benefit due to the claimant's residency status.
